name: Follow the Dollar
why_it_works: People quietly wonder whether a price is fair, and almost nobody shows them. Opening the books on one purchase feels honest and a little forbidden, which keeps people watching. Once they see how little is left at the end, the price stops feeling like a markup and starts feeling like support.

hook.pattern: Hold up the price of one purchase and promise to show exactly where every part of it goes.
examples: You paid {{price}} for this {{product}}. Follow it.
Where your {{price}} actually goes, line by line.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a hand holding the {{product}} with cash for {{price}} tucked beside it, warm moody light, {{brand}} workspace softly blurred behind
Vertical photo representing '{{slice_1_label}}' for the {{product}}, real workshop or production setting, natural light, mid shot, no logos
Vertical photo representing '{{slice_2_label}}' for the {{product}}, everyday work setting, overhead warm light, no logos
Vertical photo of a laptop screen showing a generic, unbranded checkout or fee summary, desk at night, cool screen glow

beats.purpose: what is left: animated bar shrinking to the remainder

cta: {{offer}}. Every {{product}} bought that way keeps the lights on.

craft.notes: One purchase, three cost slices, then the remainder. Build the edit around a single stacked bar that loses a chunk on every beat, so the shrinking is the story. Round numbers to whole dollars and make sure the slices plus what you keep add up exactly to the price. The carousel shows the full sum and a free way to help.

do_not: Use numbers that are not from your own books; viewers will do the math
Name or blame a real platform, distributor or store; describe the fee type instead
Play it as a guilt trip; the tone is transparency, not 'pity us'
